Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 40-year-old patient with ~3 weeks of left-sided decreased hearing and facial numbness; intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness. Same-day in-person assessment arranged; possible Bell’s palsy discussed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided hearing reduction and numbness around left ear and along left jawline for about 3 weeks; numbness present most of the time.
- Associated symptoms: Occasional left-sided ringing (tinnitus); sometimes feels dizzy when tinnitus occurs.
- Pertinent negatives: No ear discharge or ear pain; no fever; no weakness or numbness elsewhere; no difficulty swallowing or speaking; no visual changes.
- Past medical history: Nasal polyps; remote history of “labyrinthitis.”
- Medications: Nasal spray for nasal polyps (name unknown; dose/route/frequency not documented); Rennies (over-the-counter antacid) as needed; no other regular meds reported.
- Allergies: Latex. No medication allergies reported.
- Family history: Brother with neurofibromatosis (type not specified).
- Social history: Jockey; symptoms impacting training/work. Living situation statements conflict: initially states lives alone, then states lives with partner. No pets.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Left-sided hearing decrease with facial numbness and intermittent tinnitus/dizziness x ~3 weeks. Preliminary suspicion of Bell’s palsy per clinician; requires in-person neurological exam and otoscopic assessment to confirm and exclude other causes. Clinician advised condition not likely life-threatening based on history.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP clinic visit (Central London) for:
  - Full neurological examination, including cranial nerves and facial nerve assessment.
  - Otoscopic examination; consideration of focused hearing assessment if available.
- Booking process: Admin team to arrange; patient to call the support team number placed in notes after ~5 minutes to schedule at a convenient location today.
- Reassurance provided that presentation is unlikely life-threatening; definitive reassurance pending physical exam.
- No medications prescribed and no tests ordered during this telehealth visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; in-person neurological exam; otoscopy; formal hearing assessment (e.g., Rinne/Weber/audiometry); comprehensive medication reconciliation with doses/routes/frequencies; medication allergies; past surgical history; detailed social history (tobacco, alcohol, recreational drugs); recent infections/trauma exposure; pregnancy status if relevant.
- Internal conflicts: Living situation—patient stated both “lives alone” and “lives with partner” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some incomplete/inaudible segments; certain answers (e.g., ear itchiness, exact nasal spray name) not captured.
